title: Mixed Grounded Theory and Critical Discourse Analysis
short_description: A mixed GT/CDA protocol guide for combining inductive coding, discourse feature marking, actor/voice mapping, category development, relation modeling, and argument building.

phases.title: Corpus preparation
phases.description: Define what counts as data, how texts are selected, and why GT and CDA are being combined.
prompts: Why is a mixed GT/CDA design appropriate?
recommended_actions: Clarify how CDA and GT outputs will be integrated.

phases.title: Open coding
phases.description: Use open coding to name actions, processes, and meanings without losing discourse context.
prompts: What discourse feature shapes the process?
recommended_actions: Link segments to CDA features where relevant.

phases.title: Discourse feature marking
phases.description: Mark textual and discursive features such as modality, metaphor, presupposition, legitimation, and framing.
prompts: What power relation does it support or challenge?
How does it relate to a code?
recommended_actions: Link features to codes or relations.

phases.title: Actor/voice mapping
phases.description: Map actors, speaking positions, silence, agency, and evaluation.

phases.title: Axial/category development
phases.description: Develop GT categories while checking how discourse and power shape category meaning.
prompts: What CDA evidence changes the category?
recommended_actions: Assign open codes to axial codes.
Memo how CDA evidence informs GT categories.

phases.title: Relation modeling
phases.description: Connect evidence, actors, discourse features, codes, categories, memos, and research questions.
prompts: What is evidence for the claim?
Which relation is strong, weak, or uncertain?

phases.title: Theoretical memo-writing
phases.description: Write memos that explicitly connect GT categories and CDA interpretations.
prompts: What claim connects coding and discourse analysis?
recommended_actions: Link memos to codes, features, actors, and relations.

phases.title: Argument building
phases.description: Build a transparent argument from evidence, categories, discourse features, and methodological decisions.
prompts: What methodological caveat must be reported?
recommended_actions: Check claims against notes needing review.

prompts: Which methodological tradition is doing the work in this step?
What must be written into the project protocol?
How do GT categories and CDA evidence connect?

concepts.description: Combining GT and CDA requires explicit decisions about sequence, priority, integration, and reporting.
prompts: Is GT or CDA primary here?
What decision needs a protocol note?

concepts.description: A traceable connection from documents and segments to features, codes, memos, relations, and claims.
prompts: Can the claim be traced back to evidence?

sources.apa: Charmaz, K. (2014). Constructing grounded theory (2nd ed.). SAGE.
sources.note: Use for coding, comparison, memo-writing, and categories.

sources.apa: Fairclough, N. (1992). Discourse and social change. Polity.
sources.note: Use for linking text, discursive practice, and social practice.

sources.apa: van Dijk, T. A. (2008). Discourse and power. Palgrave Macmillan.
sources.note: Use for power, access, dominance, and voice.

sources.apa: Wodak, R., & Meyer, M. (Eds.). (2016). Methods of critical discourse studies (3rd ed.). SAGE.
sources.note: Use for CDA method transparency and discourse-historical considerations.

sources.apa: Miles, M. B., Huberman, A. M., & Saldaña, J. (2020). Qualitative data analysis: A methods sourcebook (4th ed.). SAGE.
sources.note: Use for displays, synthesis, and evidence-supported conclusions.

sources.apa: Saldaña, J. (2021). The coding manual for qualitative researchers (4th ed.). SAGE.
sources.note: Use for coding practices and codebook development.

sources.apa: Strauss, A., & Corbin, J. (1998). Basics of qualitative research: Techniques and procedures for developing grounded theory (2nd ed.). SAGE.
sources.note: Use for axial coding and category development.

sources.apa: Clarke, A. E. (2005). Situational analysis: Grounded theory after the postmodern turn. SAGE.
sources.note: Use for situational mapping and postmodern GT extensions.

sources.apa: Reisigl, M., & Wodak, R. (2001). Discourse and discrimination: Rhetorics of racism and antisemitism. Routledge.
sources.note: Use for DHA strategies and historical context.
